Q: How do I implement SQLCipher when using SQLiteOpenHelper? A:

Use SQLCipher exactly like your normal SQL implementation. If you are using SQLiteHelper it will create the database when you first get it:

helper.getWriteableDatabase("myPassword");

On the first call it will create the database with this password. On following calls it will only work with this password. I figured that out when I went to getWriteableDatabase( String pw ).

Use loadLibs(context) right before you call helper.getWriteableDatabase("myPassword"); the first time.

Q: What's the difference between server.servlet.session.timeout, server.servlet.session.max-age and spring.session.timeout? A:

Imagine you go to a park and the guard gives you a special stamp on your hand so he remembers you already entered. That stamp is like a session. Now, server.servlet.session.timeout it's like the guard saying, “If this child does not play or move for 10 minutes, I will forget him and remove his stamp.” So it controls how long the server remembers you if you stay inactive. Next, server.servlet.session.max-age it's like the stamp slowly fading away on your hand after some time, even if the guard is still there. This controls how long your browser keeps the session cookie. Finally, spring.session.timeout is used when instead of the guard remembering you, there is a big computer keeping track of all children. It tells the computer how long to remember you if you stop playing. So simply, one controls how long the server remembers you, one controls how long the browser keeps the cookie, and one is used when a special Spring Session system is managing everything.
